notes: Shopify storefront (robots.txt Allow:/, no Claude-specific disallow — HTTP tier sufficed, no Playwright/Chrome needed). Discovery: fetched /collections.json (201 published collections total — confirmed complete via sitemap_collections_1.xml, also 201 <loc> entries), scanned the full list for every holiday in scope (Christmas, Diwali, Halloween, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan/Rakhi, Eid, Mother's/Father's Day) plus parsed the rendered mega-menu HTML from the homepage. Only one seasonal branch exists in the site's own nav: a top-level 'Festive' menu (/collections/festive) with children Toran, Rangoli, Latkan, Shubh Labh, Votive, Festive Decor, and Christmas. No collection literally named Diwali/Rakhi/Holi/Valentine/Easter/Halloween/New-Year/Eid/Mother's-Day/Father's-Day exists — direct-guess URLs for /collections/diwali, /diwali-decor, /diwali-collection, /rakhi, /holi, /valentines-day, /new-year all 404, and none of the 201 sitemap collection <loc> entries match those terms (the one 'mother' hit was 'mother-of-pearl-collection', a material line, not Mother's Day). Confirmed absence is not a blind search-zero: internal search for 'diwali' returns 100 results (search discriminates correctly vs. a nonsense-query control returning 0), proving Diwali-relevant PRODUCTS exist, but they are not organized into a site-taxonomy category named 'Diwali' — they live inside the generic 'Festive' branch instead (see below), and per the extraction rules a search-result page is not itself a valid category row. CRITICAL DATA-QUALITY FINDING: collections.json's 'products_count' field is drastically inflated/stale for every Festive-branch collection (matches the known Shopify products_count unreliability pattern) — e.g. Festive shows API count 860 vs. real rendered/enumerated count 104; Toran 306 vs 42; Rangoli 72 vs 12; Christmas Collection 207 vs 9; Votive 104 vs 9; Festive Decor 95 vs 31; Shubh Labh 44 vs 11; Latkan 91 vs 3. For every row below I cross-checked the API count against (a) the storefront /products.json live enumeration (limit=250, page=1 returns all, page=2 returns 0) and (b) the rendered collection page's own 'N products' text — both independently agree, so the SMALLER, verified number is what's recorded as qty, not the inflated collections.json field. Site-wide catalog is ~1262 products (rendered /collections/all count), so even the largest row here (Festive Decor, 31; Festive parent, 104) is a small fraction of the catalog — no red-flag inflation. CONTENT VERIFICATION: sampled PDP body copy for a Toran product explicitly states 'ideal for Diwali, Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi, pooja ceremonies, weddings, and other festive occasions' — confirming these are genuine, occasion-specific festival decor items (diyas/toran/rangoli/shubh-labh are classic Indian festival decor types), not a generic catalog reused under a festive label. However, per the Seasonal skill's explicit boundary rule ('do not assume every Festive category means Diwali — use the site's actual context'), since the site itself never names a standalone 'Diwali' category and these items serve multiple Indian festivals (Diwali + Navratri + Ganesh Chaturthi + poojas/weddings) rather than Diwali exclusively, I kept the site's own category label 'Festive' rather than relabeling it 'Diwali'. Christmas is kept as its own distinct category since it is an unambiguous single holiday, verified via sample product titles (Christmas ornaments, frosted trees, Santa hangings, red bow ornaments — all genuinely Christmas-specific, not generic decor). No Mother's Day / Father's Day category exists anywhere on the site (checked nav, sitemap, and direct URL guesses) — correctly absent, not included. 'Festive' parent kept as a grouping row (qty/link null) since its children (summed ~117) exceed its own unique count (104), proving overlap/subset relationship rather than a separate leaf. The 'occasions' collection (0 products, 'By Occasion') and Shubh Labh's own '/occasions' page were checked and found empty/non-substantive — excluded.
